title: Chapter 436
paragraphs: Chapter 436
125. Attackers, Brothers (4)
Cold air spread like a spider's web, quickly entangling Salsu. He tried to escape, but he couldn't help but be tied up while avoiding Talaris's sword.
"Ugh…!"
Within a few seconds, Salsu was immobilized by the long-stretched ice crystals, and soon after, he could barely move his eyes within the ice.
The reason Talaris Endormai could so easily subdue a 9-star warrior was because she was Talaris Endormai.

"Heh, you're nicely frozen. Wait quietly in there until everything is settled. Don't even think about doing something ridiculous like suicide or self-destruction. You won't be able to move a finger anyway."
Leaving Salsu behind, Talaris entered the interior of Tikan and thought about where she had seen him before.
'Right, it was about 30 years ago. It was the day I went to see Chiron.'
About 30 years ago, Talaris had once visited Chiron's secret hideout.
There was only one reason for Talaris to visit Chiron at that time.
A duel.
She couldn't even remember how many times she had requested a duel. By then, Talaris had experienced at least a hundred defeats to Chiron.
That day, for some reason, her frustration surged more violently than usual after losing.
So, with the intention of ending it, she continued to cause trouble after the duel had ended.
She destroyed Chiron's secret hideout, spat out all sorts of insults at him, and just kept fighting until one of them died.
'Uh… When I think about it now, there is no such dark history. At that time, I felt like I would go crazy if I didn't do that.'
Over the past thousand years, Hidden Palace had never surpassed Runcandel's power, but it was not uncommon for Hidden Palace's ruler to possess a higher martial status than Runcandel's.
Talaris aimed for that and challenged Chiron every day. Although she never succeeded.
Anyway, Chiron showed tolerance to Talaris, who was causing trouble.
"Talaris, rather than aiming to defeat me, you should dream of Hidden Palace surpassing Runcandel."
Chiron had no reason to kill Talaris, who was almost his only friend and the one who could help him the most if he ever succumbed to 'chaos.'
However, some of the executioners at that time, who had witnessed it all, saw Talaris as a thorn in their eyes.
Her disrespectful attitude towards Chiron was an issue, as was the rumor that spread like a plague between the two. The rumor was that Chiron felt sympathy and couldn't defeat Talaris.
'Ah, I finally remember. Luton Perman, it must have been that name.'
Luton Perman.
He was the man who had just been bound by Talaris's cold air, and 30 years ago, he was the captain of the first-class executioners at a young age.
Luton and the executioners at that time believed that they had to deal with Talaris. They thought it was the way to protect Chiron's dignity and the authority of their family.
Of course, Chiron had never ordered Talaris to be attacked, but he had never ordered them not to attack her either.
That was the reason the group of executioners in Lutan's team, who were ranked 1st, ambushed Talaris.
'Back then, they rushed into the labyrinth and were beaten to death.'
At that time, Lutan and his teammates were mostly 9-star experts or close to it, but they were no match for Talaris, especially within the labyrinth.
After defeating and subduing the executioners, Talaris found their excessive loyalty to be rather endearing.
She was grateful that someone as cold as Chiron had such passionate subordinates.
In other words, Talaris didn't entirely dislike the rudeness committed by Lutan and his teammates.
Talaris did not report the executioners' misconduct to Chiron, and they continued to challenge her day and night (despite ganging up on her), just as Talaris had done to Chiron.
She considered Lutan and his teammates as aggressive, pure, and beast-like.
As a result, she even had brief romantic relationships with a few of them, including Lutan.
Chuckle, Talaris laughed at the memories that were becoming clearer.
However, she couldn't help but think with a serious expression right after.

'Judging by what he said, it seems like he lived as a nameless knight, but why did such a loyal guy end up like this? I guess the other guys who attacked the island were also made up of exiles. It doesn't seem like Chiron would have done that.'
It wasn't Chiron's way to cleanly exterminate the three tribes and leave their faces in that state.
Although the memories weren't unforgettable, she felt a bit of pity and curiosity because they weren't that bad.
'Whatever happens, it's a matter of Runcandel, not something I should interfere with. However, if possible, I'd like our son-in-law to absorb those disgraced beasts.'
Whether Jin became the head of Runcandel or the hostess of the labyrinth, as long as he absorbed them well, the exiles would have been a considerable force.
Even if the exiles were not absorbed as a force, they could be important reasons for the future when attacking the Council of Elders.
The interior of the Tichon appeared to be a battleground at first glance.

The sky was darkened by the ice of Manbing and the aura of Murakan, and underneath that, explosions were occurring as auras and magical powers mixed layer by layer (Tichon Free City had a tower-like structure).
However, contrary to its appearance, the interior was not damaged.
The greatest force of the labyrinth had been added, and thanks to the dragons that could quickly fly around and inspect the small territory, they were able to avoid harm.
Murakan and Quikantel flew between the layers, taking care of civilians who had not managed to escape.
Jin and Syris, the seven swords of the labyrinth, the Tona brothers, and Tichon's colleagues were holding back the rampaging Salsu.
Talaris quickly looked around all the layers while riding on Manbing's ice and lent her strength to those who seemed to need help.
"Son-in-law, I've found out the identity of these guys..."
Talaris approached Jin and opened her mouth to speak when she found him. However, she stopped without finishing her sentence, because it was the first time she had seen Jin in that state.
The assailants who were killing people had a nearly demonic look on their faces. Their murderous intent and venom were so deep and dense that even Talaris was taken aback.
'It's like a spitting image of my father.'
It reminded her of Chiron in his youth, when he was filled with hatred after losing his comrades.
It seemed even more sensitive than that. There were no confirmed casualties among his comrades yet.
The assailants were not all former executioners, but they were highly skilled. However, Jin easily slashed through them as if they were fallen leaves.
"These damn things, how dare they think this place is..."
Hmmm!
Jin turned his head suddenly and looked at Talaris.
Feeling her presence belatedly, he quickly regained his composure, which had been submerged in anger.
"I apologize, Talaris. I didn't hear you. Please tell me again."
"I said I found out their identities. They are Runcandel's exiles."
"I thought it could be possible. There are limited organizations capable of mobilizing mercenaries of this level..."

"Hmm. Including the guy I faced outside, some of them are likely to be former executioners. Before killing them all, if the damage to Tikan isn't too severe, it wouldn't be bad to have a conversation with them. They weren't so bad in my memory."
Jin nodded his head.
"I'll do that, Talaris."
"You looked like a mad demon just a moment ago, and now you've regained your composure quickly."
At that, Jin smiled shyly.
"It was a mistake. I knew something like this could happen, but it's not easy to control my anger when I face it directly."
What if Talaris had been absent? What if Mort couldn't use dimensional movement? What if he hadn't been in a position to hear the news directly from Kashmir and Petrolo?
Such assumptions were fueling Jin's anger.
"Fortunately, there doesn't seem to be much damage otherwise. There wasn't a single casualty in sight."
"Does that include civilians?"

"Yes. Although there was quite a lot of damage to buildings and facilities. Finish subduing them and check the exact damage. Also, since the assailants may become your swords due to their status as exiles, I recommend showing some mercy."
"Thank you, Talaris."
"Instead of thanking me, hurry up and marry my daughter."
Jin didn't answer but simply bowed his head.
After spending a night in the inner sanctum of the Hidden Palace, Jin and Syris had agreed to ignore Talaris's constant talk of marriage.
"Jin."
During the flight, Quikantel spotted Jin and called him as he descended.
"Quikantel! Is everyone safe?"
[There was no damage at the mansion. Thanks to you, Murakan, and Hidden Palace for coming right away.]
At those words, Jin felt relieved, and Quikantel and Talaris exchanged greetings with a glance.
[Thank you, 51st Hidden Palace Lord.]
"Don't mention it. I've heard that I've had connections with previous Hidden Palace Lords. Please, take care of me too."
It took 30 minutes after Jin, Murakan, and Hidden Palace's party arrived at Tikan for the terror to be completely suppressed.
There were a total of 170 assailants who attacked Tikan. In addition to the twenty people initially identified by the Tona brothers, there were fifty more who had entered from the opposite side.
After confirming their scale, Talaris concluded that even if they hadn't come in the first place, Tikan would not have been in any danger from them.
"It seems the elders of your family thought Quikantel wasn't here and sent only this many people."
If Quikantel hadn't been there and Jin hadn't provided support quickly, it would have been enough people to completely destroy Tikan.
Jin looked down at the captured assailants who were taken to the mansion.
There were Lutan Perman and another former executioner turned exile, both bound by a cold chill, and three ordinary assailants.
The rest had been killed by Jin and his comrades.
Jin asked the three ordinary assailants,
"Are you also exiles from Runcandel?"
"No."
"Don't take it too hard, I might have done the same if our positions were reversed."
Swoosh!
Jin mercilessly took their lives.
It wasn't like earlier when he was consumed by anger and swung his sword. They must have known the consequences of attacking his land, and it was only a judgment that they should pay the price.
All that was left were the two ex-executioner exiles.
Jin's gaze at them was cold.
"I can't understand how you dared to touch this place with your exile status. Tell me what the elders promised you. Or, were your family members taken hostage by those old men?"
"Our families were killed a long time ago. It was the very day we were exiled. Why, you ask, would we follow the elders' orders after being exiled, 12th generation?"
Lutan lowered his head and continued his words.
"For revenge."
